newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel warns PLO over West Bank, Gaza clashes.
newsitem.headline: Israel warns PLO over West Bank, Gaza clashes.

text.p: Israel warned the Palestinian Authority to quell a wave of anti-Israeli violence in the West Bank and Gaza Strip or risk a stronger military response.
"I don't say (the Authority) is initiating it but it must block it. That is our demand," Foreign Minister David Levy said in parliament on Wednesday.

Israeli troops, coming under a rain of petrol bombs and rocks, fired rubber-coated metal bullets and wounded 37 Palestinians in the divided West Bank town of Hebron, witnesses said. Soldiers shot dead an Arab teenager in a clash in Gaza.
"The (Palestinians) will bring us to the situation where our weaponry will have to change...I suggest they reconsider their actions," Internal Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani told Army Radio.

"We will have to alter our style and this will cause very great damage," Kahalani, who has ministerial responsibility for paramilitary Israeli border police, said in a clear threat to begin using more lethal ammunition.

The radio said Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai sent a "sharp message" to the Palestinian Authority, in charge of parts of the West Bank and Gaza, warning that Israel would be forced to use "an iron fist" if the unrest got worse.

Israeli security sources said army chief Amnon Shahak met on Wednesday on the Israel-Gaza border with Mohammad Dahlan, chief of the Palestinian Preventive Security agency in the Strip, to urge him to calm tensions.
Hours later, Israeli soldiers shot dead a 16-year-old Palestinian at a protest in Gaza against Jewish settlement expansion.

The violence was a sign of growing Palestinian frustration over a Middle East peace process deadlocked since Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu began the construction of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.
Arab anger has risen in Hebron since the discovery on storefronts on Saturday of anti-Moslem hate posters depicting the Prophet Mohammad as a pig, an animal viewed as unclean by Islam.
Israeli police said a 25-year-old Jewish woman from Jerusalem, now under arrest, pasted the posters.

"All it takes to start a fire (in Hebron) is for one crazy woman to draw a poster and distribute it," Mordechai told reporters. Israeli leaders have apologised to Palestinian political and religious officials.

While bullets flew in Gaza and in divided Hebron, Netanyahu met for 45 minutes in Jerusalem with Levy, who has threatened to quit over the way the prime minister runs the government and deals with peacemaking.
A spokesman for Netanyahu said problems remained and another meeting would be held, but gave no date.
Levy has demanded a leading role in guiding peacemaking with the Palestinians.
"I understand his thoughts and also his worries and his needs and I can assure you that we will work well together and achieve our mutual goals," Netanyahu told reporters.
Levy leads the Gesher faction, which holds five of 66 coalition seats in the 120-member parliament. If he bolts, Netanyahu will be left in control of a tenuous majority of one.

Political analysts predicted Levy would stay in the coalition for now because he was uncertain Gesher, which ran in last year's elections vowing to improve the economic standing of low-income Israelis, would fare well in a new ballot.
The opposition left-wing Meretz party said it would bring a no-confidence motion against Netanyahu in parliament next week.
"There is a war raging in Hebron and the prime minister and his ministers are preoccupied with massaging their egos," Meretz leader Yossi Sarid said.
